title: EHS Conjecture at Higher Cardinals: Failure at All Successor Alephs
description: Generalizes the Erdős-Hajnal-Szemerédi conjecture to arbitrary uncountable cardinals and proves it fails at every successor aleph ℵ_{α+1}. The limit cardinal case remains open. Extends the Lambie-Hanson (2020) disproof of Erdős Problem #110 via Todorcevic's walks on ordinals framework.

meta.author: Lambie-Hanson (2020), Todorcevic (walks on ordinals)

mathlibDependencies.description: Simple graphs on a vertex type
The aleph function mapping ordinals to infinite cardinals

originalContributions: GeneralizedEHSConjecture: parametric formulation of the EHS conjecture for arbitrary cardinal κ
Proof that the conjecture fails at every successor aleph ℵ_{α+1} (generalized_ehs_fails_all_successor_alephs)
No-universal-bound theorem: no single F works across all uncountable graphs
Identification of limit cardinals as the genuinely open case
meta.assumptions: 1 axiom: successor_cardinal_counterexample (generalization via Todorcevic walks). The ℵ₁ case (Lambie-Hanson 2020) is proved as a special case at α=0. All 8 theorems derive from this single axiom.

overview.historicalContext:
**Higher Cardinals and the EHS Conjecture**

The Erdős-Hajnal-Szemerédi conjecture (1982) asked about ℵ₁-chromatic graphs specifically. After Lambie-Hanson's 2020 disproof, the natural follow-up is: what happens at ℵ₂, ℵ₃, and beyond?

The key technique — Todorcevic's walks on ordinals — uses the combinatorial structure of ordinal sequences (C-sequences) to construct incompatible colorings. On successor ordinals ω_{α+1}, C-sequences have the right properties for the construction. On limit ordinals, the situation is fundamentally different.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question**

Does the Erdős-Hajnal-Szemerédi conjecture fail at ALL uncountable cardinals, or only at successor alephs?

**Known**: The conjecture fails at every successor aleph ℵ_{α+1} (for all ordinals α), via generalized walk constructions.

**Open**: The limit cardinal case (ℵ_ω, ℵ_{ω₁}, etc.) remains unresolved. The proof techniques for successor cardinals do not directly transfer.
overview.text: Generalizes the EHS conjecture failure from ℵ₁ to all successor alephs. The limit cardinal case remains open.
overview.proofStrategy:
**The Formalization**

1. Defines GeneralizedEHSConjecture(κ) parametrized by any cardinal κ
2. Proves the ℵ₁ case from Lambie-Hanson's counterexample
3. Axiomatizes successor cardinal counterexamples (from Todorcevic walks)
4. Proves the conjecture fails at every ℵ_{α+1}
5. Proves no universal bounding function exists
6. Documents the limit cardinal open question
keyInsights: The EHS conjecture fails at EVERY successor aleph, not just ℵ₁
Each cardinal level has its own independent counterexample
Todorcevic's walks on ordinals provide the unifying construction technique
Limit cardinals are structurally different — C-sequences behave differently
No single function F can bound n-chromatic subgraph sizes across all uncountable graphs

sections.title: Core Definitions
sections.summary: Restated definitions from the parent problem
sections.mathContext: Restates the core graph coloring infrastructure: proper colorings, $k$-colorability, induced subgraphs, chromatic numbers, and the finite $n$-chromatic subgraph predicate $\text{HasFiniteNChromaticSubgraph}\,G\,n\,b$. These are identical to the parent Erdős #110 formalization.

sections.title: Generalized EHS Conjecture
sections.summary: The conjecture parametrized by any cardinal κ
sections.mathContext: Defines $\text{GeneralizedEHSConjecture}(\kappa)$: for every graph $G$ with $\chi(G) = \kappa$, there exist $F : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $N_0$ such that for all $n \geq N_0$, $G$ has an $n$-chromatic subgraph on $\leq F(n)$ vertices. The original EHS conjecture is the special case $\kappa = \aleph_1$.

sections.title: The ℵ₁ Case (Known Disproof)
sections.mathContext: Axiomatizes Lambie-Hanson's counterexample and proves $\neg\text{GeneralizedEHSConjecture}(\aleph_1)$ by extracting the counterexample graph and deriving a contradiction with any proposed bound $F$.

sections.title: Higher Successor Cardinals
sections.summary: Failure at all successor alephs via ordinal walks
sections.mathContext: Axiomatizes the existence of counterexamples at every successor aleph $\aleph_{\alpha+1}$, based on generalizing Lambie-Hanson's technique via Todorcevic's walks on $\omega_{\alpha+1}$. The main theorem `generalized_ehs_fails_all_successor_alephs` shows $\forall \alpha, \neg\text{GeneralizedEHSConjecture}(\aleph_{\alpha+1})$.

sections.title: Structural Analysis
sections.mathContext: The `CounterexampleGraph` structure packages: (1) $\chi(G) = \kappa$ exactly, and (2) $G$ defeats all proposed bounds $F$. The theorem `counterexample_exists_at_successor` shows such structures exist at every successor level, and `counterexample_implies_failure` shows any counterexample implies conjecture failure.

sections.title: The Limit Cardinal Question
sections.summary: Open question: what happens at ℵ_ω, etc.?
sections.mathContext: For limit cardinals $\aleph_\lambda$ where $\lambda$ is a limit ordinal, the EHS conjecture's status is genuinely unknown. C-sequences on limit ordinals have fundamentally different combinatorial properties, and the walk-based constructions do not directly transfer. This is defined as `LimitCardinalEHSOpen` to mark it as an open problem.

sections.title: No Universal Bounding Function
sections.summary: No single F works for all uncountable graphs
sections.mathContext: A stronger result than individual cardinal failures: there is no single $F : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for ALL graphs $G$ with $\chi(G) \geq \aleph_1$, the function $F$ bounds $n$-chromatic subgraph sizes. Proved directly from the Lambie-Hanson counterexample.

sections.title: Summary
sections.mathContext: The summary theorem `erdos_110_oq_03_summary` combines three results: (1) failure at $\aleph_1$, (2) failure at all successor alephs $\aleph_{\alpha+1}$, and (3) no universal bounding function. Together these give a comprehensive negative answer to the higher cardinal question for all successor levels.

conclusion.summary: The EHS conjecture fails comprehensively at all successor alephs, not just ℵ₁. Each successor cardinal ℵ_{α+1} admits its own counterexample graph via Todorcevic's walks on ordinals. No universal bounding function exists. The limit cardinal case is genuinely open and structurally different.
conclusion.implications:
1. **Complete successor cardinal failure**: The EHS conjecture is not salvageable by moving to higher cardinals

2. **Todorcevic walks as universal tool**: The walk technique unifies counterexamples across all successor levels

3. **Limit cardinals as frontier**: The genuine open question is at ℵ_ω, ℵ_{ω₁}, and other limit alephs

4. **No universal bound**: Even without fixing a cardinal, no single F works for all uncountable graphs
openQuestions: Does the EHS conjecture hold or fail at limit alephs (ℵ_ω, ℵ_{ω₁})?
Is the limit cardinal answer independent of ZFC?
